name: Oneflow
summary: Digital contract platform for the full lifecycle — create, negotiate, e-sign and archive interactive contracts, with AI-assisted contract features and CRM/HR/ATS integrations (HubSpot, Salesforce), sold per user on annual billing.
best_for: sales and legal teams with real contract volume who want the full lifecycle — creating, negotiating, e-signing and archiving interactive contracts — in one platform with CRM integrations
skip_if: you just need signatures (a per-seat e-sign tool costs a fraction), or you cannot commit to annual billing at €250 a month
honest_knock: The entry is €250 a month on annual billing — €3,000 a year committed before you've sent your first contract — and the rest of the ladder lives in a sales conversation. If you only need documents signed, dedicated e-sign tools start at roughly a tenth of that.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user a month billed annually, 5-user minimum (floor €250/month)

plans.name: Business

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes:
(price re-verified 2026-09-18 and again on 2026-10-05 against oneflow.com/pricing/; read from a Dutch connection, and the page sells in EUR, GBP, NOK, SEK and USD — these are the EUR figures) Business is €50 per user per month, billed annually, for teams starting at five users, so €250 a month is the floor. Oneflow now states that floor itself rather than leaving it to be multiplied out: the page says the entry-level plan includes 5 seats and starts at €250 per month, billed annually. That is the whole public price list. Enterprise starts at ten users and goes through a sales call, and the trial runs 14 days without a card. A free contract-template library is available without an account.

Annual is not a discount option, it is the only option, and the page now says so in its own FAQ under “Why can you only pay on an annual basis?” — the answer cites long-term value, secure deployments and dedicated onboarding. Several features sit behind a ($) marker even on the plan that lists them, meaning a paid add-on rather than an unavailable feature: eID signature on Business, redirect-after-sign on Enterprise and, read 5 October 2026, the two Beta AI features, AI Review & Insights and AI Insights Premium, on both plans. On 18 September the Enterprise card still listed AI review and AI insights without that marker.
